chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say:
There is no harm in the leftover of a mouse, if it has drunk from the vessel, that one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) from it.

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel or container holding the water
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: the leftover remainder of drink or water after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.يُشْرَبَ: to be drunk or used for drinking

ai.seo_question: Can water be used for drinking and wudu (ablution) after a mouse has drunk from the vessel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the remaining water in a vessel from which a mouse has drunk is not considered problematic for use. It indicates that such water may still be used both for drinking and for wudu (ablution), reflecting a ruling in ritual purity.
